meta.expansionNote: v1.0 had 20 activities per level. This pack expands to the standard 30 slots + 2 checkpoints. The 12 added slots are V8, G3, G4, G5, L2, R1, R4, W2, S2, S4, S6, S7 (plus CP1). All v1.0 content is retained inside those slots.
meta.reviewConnection: Unit 3 completes the language of Review 1 (Units 1-3). The Boss pool deliberately mixes Do/Does, So do I / Neither do I, wears vs is wearing, want vs wants and Does...taste good, because those are the contrasts a learner confuses across the first three units.

R4.passage: Lots of people like pizza, but where does it come from? Pizza is popular in many places now, and people make it with a flat bread, then put other kinds of food on top. The word pizza comes from Italy. The name of one of the first pizzas in the world is Pizza Margherita, and it was made for a queen. It has white cheese, red tomatoes and green basil, which are the colors of the Italian flag. So the pizza is not only food; it is also a picture of a country. Pizza Margherita looks good and it tastes good, too. Now people all over the world eat pizza, and many people cook it in a special pizza oven because a very hot oven makes the bread crisp. It tastes delicious.

one sentence about another person's order
one negative sentence with doesn't or don't
one sentence saying whether you would go back
checklist: One sentence with looks, smells or tastes

S1.prompt: Say each line before the model appears. Listen for the endings.

items.model: The chips look good, but the fish smells bad.
She wants some ice cream after lunch.

S2.prompt: Chunk drill. Three times each, then once at full speed.

S3.prompt: Ask and answer. Full sentences, and use because at least once.

items.q: What do you want to eat, and why?
Does anyone in your family dislike a food because of how it smells?
Compare two foods on a menu. Which looks better?
What would you refuse to eat, and how would you say it politely?

S4.prompt: Describe the table for 45 seconds. Compare two dishes and use one negative sentence.
prompts: One dish you would refuse and why

S5.prompt: Perform the dialogue as all three characters, with a different voice for each.
S5.extra: Then answer: why is the joke funny? Use all three senses in your answer.

S6.prompt: Personal response. Three questions, full sentences, at least one reason each.

items.q: Is food in your country mostly healthy? Explain.
Why do people say food tastes better when it looks good?
Which is more important in a restaurant: the food or the service? Explain.

S7.prompt: Speak for 60 seconds: My Perfect Meal. Cover all four points; the checklist stays on screen.
scaffold: For my perfect meal I want ___, ___ and ___.
My ___ wants ___, and so do I.
selfCheck: I used two of the three senses

CP1.prompt: Halfway checkpoint. Six items drawing on everything so far.

items.why: The others are taste adjectives.

items.q: Ask a question with Does...taste...? and answer it.

BOSS.prompt: The Pizza Party. Eight items across all six skills, then a 45-second spoken response.

items.sentence: The chips ___ good but the fish ___ bad.
Does he wants salad, and neither do she?

items.audio: Everyone is happy except me. Emma has chips and they look good. Brian has meat and it smells delicious. I wanted the fish, but it smelled bad and it tasted bad too. So I am eating bread.

passes.q: What is the speaker eating instead?

items.q: Tap the sentence that explains why a very hot oven matters for pizza.
items.answer: Now people all over the world eat pizza, and many people cook it in a special pizza oven because a very hot oven makes the bread crisp.
Neither Brian nor Emma likes fish.

items.prompt: Type the word that means 'very good to eat'.

items.q: Speak for 45 seconds: a meal you remember, how it looked, smelled and tasted, and whether you would order it again.

lines.speaker: Grandpa
lines.text: I'm tired! I need a break.

lines.speaker: Brian
lines.text: I want fish, please. It looks good.

lines.speaker: Brian
lines.text: It looks bad. It smells bad.

core.q: Why does Brian choose fish at first?

challenging.q: What changes between Brian's first sentence and his last?
options: The food looks good, then looks bad
Brian changes his mind about fish
challenging.answer: The food looks good, then looks bad

challenging.q: Which three senses does the story use?

phonics.note: Optional pronunciation card inside the Speaking station.
phonics.note2: The trap is that ch, sh and th all appear in the unit's own vocabulary: chips (ch), shirt (sh), three (th). Say them in one breath group so the contrast is audible.

speechScoring.reuse: Same engine as Units 1, 2 and 4: browser Web Speech API, keyword coverage, bands only, never a numeric grade.
additions: This unit introduces three new spoken forms to normalise: 'wants' (apply the same soft treatment as Unit 2's -s: accept 'want' at Easy, require it at Challenging), 'looks / smells / tastes' (the -s is the teaching point), and 'doesn't' (accept 'does not').
The three-sense verbs are easily confused in speech: if the learner says 'smell' where 'tastes' was expected, show the word rather than failing the item.

review1Connection.note: This unit completes Review 1 (Units 1-3). These contrasts are the natural Boss pool for Unit 3 and are worth wiring into the mixed checkpoint.

distractorContrasts.b: He is wearing a hat today.

review1Connection.bonusIdea: These six items would make an excellent standalone Review Island covering Units 1-3.

selfAssessment.intro: There are no right answers here. Be honest — it helps you.

vocabulary.easy: I can name some foods and drinks in English.
vocabulary.core: I can name foods and say how they taste.
vocabulary.challenging: I can use taste words precisely and talk about where food comes from.

grammar.easy: I can say what I want.
grammar.core: I can use want and wants, and ask with does.
grammar.challenging: I can use look, smell and taste with the right endings.

listening.easy: I can hear a food or drink word and find it.
listening.core: I can understand someone ordering food.
listening.challenging: I can follow a longer description of a meal and catch how someone feels.

reading.easy: I can read a short text about food.
reading.core: I can find facts about food in a text.
reading.challenging: I can understand an opinion and a surprising detail.

writing.easy: I can write one sentence about a meal.
writing.core: I can write an order and describe how the food tastes.
writing.challenging: I can write a short review with a reason.

speaking.easy: I can say what I want to eat.
speaking.core: I can order politely and ask how something tastes.
speaking.challenging: I can describe a meal using all three senses.

selfAssessment.notePrompt: One thing I want to get better at.
